page: Amazon Web Services gr6.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance provisioned on the Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, configured with 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is set to 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, yielding an expanded 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM based on the Ada Lovelace microarchitecture. Local ephemeral storage includes a 600 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional machine learning inference performance powered by the onboard NVIDIA L4 accelerator. In language model evaluations, prompt processing achieved 12,183.3 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 2,301.81 tokens per second on a medium 7B model, placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Text generation hit 472.77 tokens per second on the 135M model and 54.0 tokens per second on the 7B model. CPU-bound throughput shows solid capabilities, registering a strong single-core stress-ng result of 2,992.68 and a multi-core score of 23,942.61. General computational benchmarks fall in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,180.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23,701.44.

Hardware tradeoffs manifest primarily in uncached memory write throughput, which scored 22.83 GB/sec in 256 MB tests, sitting in the bottom 25 percent. The system does not support AVX-512 extensions. Cost efficiency is balanced qualitatively by combining dedicated GPU acceleration, large system RAM, and fast local NVMe storage into a single host footprint, minimizing the need for multi-instance distributed coordination for mid-tier inference. These parameters make AWS gr6.4xlarge well matched for graphics rendering, generative AI model serving, real-time video processing, and memory-intensive analytical workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services gr6.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 3.4 GHz and 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It integrates a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU offering 22 GB of VRAM along with 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 10 Gbps baseline networking on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier LLM inference performance, reaching 12,183.3 tokens per second for prompt processing on small models and 54.0 tokens per second for text generation on 7B models. Compute and decompression performance track within middle percentiles, though uncached memory write throughput remains lower. AWS gr6.4xlarge provides a resource-dense profile suitable for AI inference, real-time graphics rendering, and memory-heavy analytical tasks.
